subject: best of both worlds for located exceptions?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: best of both worlds for located exceptions?
parts:
Here's what I came up with. It doesn't require any policy
on Stan code and will use RTTI to create an appropriately
typed exception (that is, catchable by the nested exception
type) if it's in the standard library (option 1), falling back
on std::exception for other types (option 2).

I've attached the code and the test to show how it works
on its own. I also pushed to feature/issue-1195-runtime-error-lines
in case anyone wants to run the test.

My lingering uncertainty is whether it's safe to store the
nested type as a const reference and return it the same way
from the getter. It'd be easy enough to copy the nested exception
and return it by value rather than by reference. (One of the
current tests for reference equality will fail, though.)

My plan is to wrap the code blocks of all relevant functions
and the constructor as:

int line__ = -1;
try {
...run updating line number...
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
throw_located_exception(e,line__);
}

If the exception e is an instance of any of the std library
exception types, the rethrown exception will be catchable
by its type E or by located_exception<E>. I could add some
Boost types to the parade.

I also built in the inspection with RTTI for good measure
in case someone wants to just catch std::exception and use
RTTI to inspect the type of the nested exception and get it
dynamically cast to a given type.

I learned a lot about exceptions building this thing today!

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: best of both worlds for located exceptions?
parts:
Still not compiling without -std=c++11

goodrich@T540p:/tmp$ clang++-3.6 -fsyntax-only located_exception_test.cpp
In file included from located_exception_test.cpp:1:
./located_exception.hpp:80:24: error: no member named 'to_string' in namespace 'std'
                + std::to_string(line)
                  ~~~~~^

instead do

            + static_cast<std::ostringstream*>( &(std::ostringstream() << line) )->str()

Ben

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] best of both worlds for located exceptions?
parts:
I read over the code quickly and two small things:

1. In located_exception::get() I think it should be a dynamic cast, not a static one.
2. In throw_located_exception() if it falls through to the std::exception case, it might be worth emitting a warning with the typeid of the exception that was thrown so that we know when this case gets hit.

Otherwise it looks great!

Cheers,
Marcus
